title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (Dec 2026)
author: Maya Chen
summary: Comprehensive product document that combines the product overview, PRD requirements, design specifications, roadmap and themes for the next 6-12 months, pricing and packaging guidance, and the latest release notes (Dec 2026). Serves as the canonical reference for PM, Eng, Sales, and GTM teams for planning, implementation, and launch activities.
body:
Overview

Short intro
Unified Inference is Redwood Inference’s core product line that provides a single API and operational model for running LLM inference across Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. This document consolidates the product overview, prioritized requirements (PRD), key design specifications, roadmap and themes for the next 6-12 months, pricing and packaging guidance, and the latest release notes (Dec 2026).

Goals
- Provide a single developer experience for text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, and structured output across deployment modes.
- Deliver predictable latency and cost controls for production workloads.
- Enable enterprise-grade controls (SLA, VPC, KMS) for regulated customers.
- Reduce unit inference cost by 30% for typical web workloads through batching, caching and quantization profiles.

Target personas
- ML Engineers integrating model inference into product features.
- Platform/Backend Engineers responsible for scale and reliability.
- Product Managers and Solution Engineers evaluating performance and pricing trade-offs.

High-level success metrics (KPIs)
- Time to first API call (onboard) <= 30 minutes for Hosted API.
- 95th percentile p99 generation latency <= 300ms for short-form (<=128 tokens) hosted models.
- Unit cost reduction >= 25% for customers adopting Optimize recommendations.
- NPS for enterprise customers >= 45 for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Product Requirements (PRD) - prioritized
1) Core API parity (Must)
- Text generation: streaming + structured output support.
- Chat API with system/user/assistant roles and function/tool calling.
- Embeddings: batch and streaming ingestion with stable vector dims.
- Authentication & rate limits: API keys, per-route quotas, usage metering.

2) Deterministic performance controls (Must)
- Batching controls with per-route batch size and max wait time.
- KV cache / prefix cache with TTL and per-customer size limits.
- Quantization profile support (int8/int4) with model compatibility map.

3) Enterprise controls (Must)
- VPC peering and Private control plane option.
- KMS/HSM integration for key management.
- Audit logging with 90-day retention (configurable).
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated customers with incident playbooks.

4) Observability & quality (Should)
- Token-level cost and latency breakdown in Console.
- Per-prompt/eval regression alerting tied to golden prompt sets.
- Tracing hooks and request sampling for debugging.

5) Cost & optimization toolkit (Could)
- Automatic batching/caching recommendations.
- Model variant routing for cost-sensitive fallbacks.

Requirements table (condensed)
| Requirement ID | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
| RI-001 | Must | eng-serving-runtime | Streaming generation + function calling passes integration tests and latency targets |
| RI-002 | Must | eng-platform | Per-route batching controls implemented and can be configured via Console/Config API |
| RI-010 | Must | security-and-compliance | KMS integration documented and tested in Private deployment labs |
| RI-020 | Should | product | Console shows token-level cost breakdown with 1-hour freshness |

Design specifications (summary)
1) API & SDK design - API paths: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank.
- Streaming protocol: server-sent events (SSE) for HTTP; websocket option in roadmap.
- Backwards-compatible params: keep 'max_tokens', 'temperature', 'top_p' but introduce 'response_profile' for structured outputs.

2) Model catalog & routing
- Models have structured metadata: model_id, quantization_profile, compatible_kernels, latency_profile, cost_score (internal).
- Smart routing policy engine supports: latency_priority, cost_priority, region_affinity, enterprise_fallback.

3) Runtime & performance knobs
- Batching: continuous batching with knobs: max_batch_size, max_wait_ms, preferred_kernel.
- Caching: prefix-KV cache, per-customer namespace, eviction LRU with TTL.
- Quantization: support for int8 and int4 profiles; offline quality validation harness required before publicizing profiles.

4) Observability & tracing
- Token-level metrics emitted to Console with enrichment: model_id, customer_id, route, request_id.
- Error taxonomy: malformed_prompt, model_timeout, downstream_failure with standard remediation guidance.

Data model (brief)
- Request:{ method, route, model_id, customer_id, prompt_tokens, config_flags }
- Response:{ request_id, tokens[], latency_ms, model_version, cost_tokens }

Roadmap & themes (next 12 months)
- Q1 2027: "Developer-first parity" - complete SDK parity for Python/Node/Go, stable Streaming + function calling.
- Q2 2027: "Reliability & Ops" - Dedicated SLA rollouts, advanced Console traces, rollout automation.
- Q3 2027: "Cost & Optimize" - Redwood Optimize v3: automatic policy suggestions, model-variant routing, and quantization marketplace.
- Q4 2027: "Enterprise & Compliance" - Expanded Private on-prem package, SOC2 re-audit, expanded EU/APAC region compliance artifacts.

Roadmap themes explanation
- Developer-first parity: remove friction for product teams to migrate from experimental to production.
- Cost-aware serving: expose levers and automation so customers can control unit economics without manual tuning.
- Enterprise readiness: authentication, auditable workflows, and deterministic behavior under load.

Pricing & packaging notes
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing with separate rates for generation tokens and embedding units.
- Dedicated: commit-based reserved capacity with monthly minimums and guaranteed throughput.
- Private: platform license + per-node fee, professional services for on-prem installation.

Pricing tiers (example)
- Developer (Hosted free tier): 100k tokens/month free, pay-as-you-go afterwards.
- Growth: $X per million tokens + priority support, recommended for SMBs.
- Enterprise: custom committed pricing for Dedicated & Private with 12-month term and SLA.

Packaging guidance
- Bundle Optimize trials (1 month) with Dedicated POCs to demonstrate 20-30% unit-cost savings.
- Offer migration credits for customers moving from self-hosted inference to Redwood Dedicated for first 3 months.

Commercial guardrails
- Minimum contract size for Dedicated: $25k/month recommended.
- Discounting guided by % of annual committed spend; approvals required from finance for >20% discounts.

Release notes - v3.8.0 (2026-12-06)
- Highlights:
  - Streaming chat API: improved stability and SSE reconnect support (ENG-4921).
  - Per-route batching controls: max_batch_size and max_wait_ms now configurable via Console (PLT-513).
  - Prefix KV cache: initial GA with per-customer namespaces and TTL enforcement (RUNTIME-587).
  - Quantization profiles: int8 profiles added for redwood-llama-7B and redwood-llama-13B with compatibility docs (ML-622).

- Bug fixes:
  - Fixed incorrect token accounting for embeddings in certain batched flows (BILL-338).
  - Resolved race in model routing where region-affinity fallback could route to unsupported quantized variant (ROUTE-404).

- Migration notes for customers:
  1) If you rely on embeddings cost reports, please re-run the billing reconciliation job after Dec 10; billing patch will be applied to historical data.
  2) For Private deployments using older runtime images (<=2026.09), upgrade to runtime-2026.11 before enabling int8 quantization.

Rollout plan (v3.8)
1) Canary: internal + 5 beta customers (Dec 6-10) with monitoring dashboards and rollback playbooks.
2) Gradual: 20% traffic ramp over 48 hours (Dec 11-13).
3) Full: complete global rollout (Dec 15) if no regression alerts.

SLOs & monitoring
- API availability SLO: 99.9% for Dedicated customers.
- Token-level latency SLO (short-form): p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 400ms for supported hosted models.
- Error budget policy: automatic traffic diversion to fallback model if error budget < 10% for a given route.

Ownership & contacts
- Product owner: Maya Chen (product).
- Engineering: Runtime lead: Diego Alvarez; Platform lead: Hannah Lee.
- Security/compliance: Priya Nair.

Appendix: acceptance test checklist (short)
1) API compatibility tests pass for all semver variants.
2) Performance harnesses show p95/p99 within targets under 2x expected production QPS.
3) Console shows token-level cost breakdown in staging with sample traffic.
4) Dedicated SLA verification: failover, autoscaling, and audit log delivery validated.
